assumptions: The beachhead is limited to active EPC sites with an agreed M&V plan and meaningful recurring settlement work, not the full population of buildings needing modernization.
A qualified and appropriately independent engineering reviewer signs or certifies calculation packs; neither the founder nor the software claims professional verification.
Both contract parties authorize the evidence-room governance, source data, and adjustment process even when an owner, lender, or facilitator is the commercial payer.
Expert-review fees are separately scoped or passed through, and the stated software pricing must be supported by governance and workflow value beyond calculation tools.
A facilitator or auditor owns domain-facing exceptions and meetings so the founder can operate within the stated part-time capacity before traction.
evidence_needed_for_higher_score: Paid governed-site pilots need to document current report and dispute costs, dual-party acceptance, authorized data completeness, reviewer hours and liability terms, reduction in revision cycles, one-reporting-cycle payback, annual contribution margin after expert work, and a verified count of active EPC sites controlled by reachable channel partners.

factors.name: Core insight
factors.rationale: The candidate correctly rejects an autonomous savings oracle and instead targets the missing governance layer around frozen plans, data lineage, adjustments, uncertainty, dual-party visibility, and expert sign-off. That is a coherent response to both transparent M&V requirements and the documented need for human engineering judgment, though it is an execution insight rather than a protected discovery.

factors.name: Customer pain and willingness to pay
factors.rationale: Errors or disputes in guaranteed-savings settlements can have material financial and trust consequences across a multi-year contract, and repeat reporting creates a plausible workflow need. Direct evidence does not establish dispute frequency, revision labor, budget ownership, or willingness to pay; the Polish model already assigns reporting and corrections to the ESCO, and established tools and facilitators may be sufficient.

factors.name: Business model and economics
factors.rationale: Per-site setup and recurring fees can benefit from multi-year contracts, and separately pricing qualified review is economically sensible. The proposed 700 PLN monthly software fee must overcome a CAD 869 annual calculation alternative, while the 62% margin, 88% retention, review burden, procurement cost, one-cycle payback, and path to 350 sites are unobserved; the near-full use of available capital adds downside before validation.

factors.name: Market and beachhead
factors.rationale: Polish and CEE facilitators, independent auditors, and lenders managing smaller EPC portfolios form a logically bounded initial segment. The cited 125000 buildings measure modernization need rather than EPC contracts or software budgets, and the number of active paid sites in the proposed beachhead is unknown, so economic sufficiency is not established.

factors.name: Competitive position and domination potential
factors.rationale: A co-visible, contract-bound evidence record could become a settlement control point once named in the M&V plan. KAPE already bundles monitoring and settlement control with legal and technical services, experienced auditors hold the trust relationships, and RETScreen and EnergyCAP cover core calculations, making domination difficult without exclusive channel adoption.

factors.name: Expansion potential
factors.rationale: A proven governance workflow can expand from Polish public EPCs into private portfolios, lenders, additional CEE markets, other facilitators, and adjacent performance-based retrofit contracts. The common pattern is reusable, but expansion remains dependent on local contracts, reviewer networks, and data access rather than being frictionless software replication.

factors.name: Defensibility and durability
factors.rationale: Frozen M&V versions, approved adjustments, source-data lineage, reviewer workflows, and a long-lived contract record can create meaningful switching costs and accumulated operating knowledge. Confidentiality may block cross-site data reuse, expert services are replicable, and incumbents or facilitators can add similar evidence workflows, so the durability is moderate and conditional.

factors.name: Strength of advantage
factors.rationale: Dual-party visibility, reproducible adjustments, uncertainty disclosure, and reviewer-signed packs could materially improve trust and revision speed compared with disconnected spreadsheets or calculation-only tools. There is no comparative evidence that this process is faster, cheaper, or more acceptable than current facilitator and auditor practice, and mandatory human judgment limits pure automation advantage.

factors.name: Timing and momentum
factors.rationale: EU requirements emphasize transparent M&V, public bodies must assess EPC feasibility in relevant renovations, and Poland has a substantial building-modernization need. These are supportive forces, but they do not mandate independent software and the supplied evidence does not show rapid EPC adoption or a near-term procurement wave.

factors.name: Distribution
factors.rationale: White-label partnerships with facilitators, auditors, lenders, and metering platforms are credible routes to portfolio access and avoid camera-led marketing. The budget owner is unknown, KAPE-like facilitators already bundle the service, and dual-party approval plus public procurement creates slow, relationship-heavy, multi-stakeholder sales that fit the founder poorly.

factors.name: Execution and risks
factors.rationale: Baseline modeling, anomaly detection, uncertainty, and lineage fit the founder, and professional judgment can in principle be delegated. Reliable context data, authorized multi-party access, qualified reviewer availability, security, procurement, professional liability, non-routine events, and acceptance disputes create substantial operational complexity for a part-time founder without M&V credentials.

highest_value_structural_change: Make the facilitator or lender the portfolio sponsor and require the evidence-room protocol in new EPC M&V plans, with both parties approving governance and a pre-contracted independent reviewer pool; this converts neutrality from a vendor claim into a contractual workflow and creates portfolio-level distribution and switching costs.
main_structural_strength: The product places a reproducible, versioned evidence record between contract parties while preserving expert judgment, creating a more credible governance wedge than either an autonomous model or another savings calculator.
primary_score_limiter: The addressable EPC-site base, software budget owner, willingness to pay, and reviewer economics are all unknown, while neutrality requires multi-party adoption that makes distribution and implementation unusually difficult.
strongest_disconfirming_evidence: No rule mandates a separate software service; the Polish model assigns reporting to the ESCO, KAPE already bundles settlement control, and low-cost RETScreen plus established EnergyCAP capabilities constrain standalone software value.
